# `product/` — Product Sub-Wiki (L1)

## Inclusion test

**Does this describe the product we offer — as opposed to the work of producing it?**

If yes, it belongs here. Product holds the offering: what it is, who it is for, what it does, and the commitments about its shape. The *work* of producing it — what is scheduled, what was decided, what is at risk — is `governance/`.

## Layer position

Product is **L1**: it may cite `domain/` and nothing else, and is cited by every layer below it.

The single-ancestor constraint is the whole discipline of this layer. A product page that needs to link a surface, a component, a runbook or a price is telling you one of two things — either the content is not L1, or the fact it wants is one the deeper page should be citing *upward* instead.

## In scope

A subdir is created when a page type appears there for the first time; do not create empty subdirs speculatively. A freshly scaffolded sub-wiki therefore contains none of them, which is the expected state rather than a broken scaffold.

The page types homed here, exhaustively — the boundary, not an illustration of it. The machine-readable copy of the **Page type** column is `page-type-homes.json`, held to this list by a drift guard. The **Subdir** column is held by a different artifact — each type's own template states its home on its `Lives at:` line, and a second guard compares that line against this table. No JSON encodes a subdir; editing one of the two without the other is what the guard reports.

| Subdir | Page type | What goes here |
|---|---|---|
| `app-base.md` | `app-base` | The application base — the infrastructure no deliverable owns; the singleton infra pages attribute to via `realizes:`. |
| `modules/` | `product-module` | A deliverable (application or library), an area of one, or a page describing shared content — a named grouping of related features, plus its feature table of contents; each module's page sits beside the directory holding its areas, `modules/storefront.md` beside `modules/storefront/`. |
| `features/<module>/` | `feature` | The problem, user story, and capability-level acceptance criteria for one feature. |
| `flows/<module>/` | `task-flow` | The ordered steps for one task and its task-scoped acceptance criteria — the behavioral contract a `test-scenario` verifies. |
| `entities/<module>/` | `data-model-entity` | Our logical data-model entity — the `## Data model` shape a feature's data acts on. The industry concept is a `domain-object` in `domain/`. |
| `algorithms/` | `algorithm` | A computation the product defines — how a metric, index or score is derived. |
| `prds/` | `prd` | Problem, evidence, success metrics, prioritized requirements. Declares itself a living document. |
| `positioning/` | `value-proposition` | What we promise, to whom, and why it beats the alternatives — **and which persona we target**, which is a commitment rather than a fact. |
| `pr-faqs/` | `pr-faq` | The PR-FAQ. Its gate function is a decision, but its body is the offering, so it stays here; a separately-recorded fund/no-fund deliberation is a `daci-record` in `governance/` citing this page. |
| `catalogs/` | `catalog` | A governed coded vocabulary of *ours* — roles, notification events, statuses — **and the entitlement tiers**: the tier names and what each gates. Prices and packaging stay in `gtm/`. |
| `concepts/` | `concept` | A speculative or cross-cutting product idea. Speculative features are always `concept` here, never `domain/`, because the subject is our product. |
| `personas/` | `persona` | A person-type our own product definition creates — the operator of a surface we built. A person-type the industry has independently of us is a `persona` in `domain/`. |

## Explicitly out of scope

- **Roadmaps, OKR cycles, prioritization rounds, risk registers, decision records, retrospectives** — all `governance/`. They record the work, not the offering, and nothing constrains what they may cite, which is why they sit at the bottom rather than here.
- **Who the industry's user is** — a person-type the industry has independently of us is a `persona` in `domain/`, because it is a fact about the world; only the ones our own product definition creates are homed here. *Which* of the industry's we target is a commitment and folds into `value-proposition` here.
- **Prices, packaging, discounting** — `gtm/`. The entitlement-tier `catalog` here is what an L1 feature, an L2 pricing surface or an L3 billing component resolves a tier against; the `pricing-model` cites that catalog downward.
- **Analysis of external subjects** — `comparison`, `synthesis`, `source-summary`, `interview-debrief` are all `domain/`. Author the analysis there and cite it.
- **How it is built** — `engineering/`. **What it looks like** — `design/`.

## Owner

The product function owns this sub-wiki. Product authors the persona, feature, and flow pages; reviews mirror summaries; and signs off on canonical claims. Everyone else reads it — engineering grounds implementation in product intent, design grounds UX in the journeys that name its flows, and governance cites it when scheduling or deciding about it. **Authorship is not ownership:** GTM authors the `value-proposition` that product owns.

## Default origination mode: `originate`

Product intent is what an agent acts on, and the wiki is canonical wherever that is true — which is why L1 originates while L5 mirrors. The planning tools stay canonical for the work: Linear owns the tickets and their status, Notion owns the long-form drafts. What the product IS — the features, the flows, the entities, the value proposition — is defined here, and a page that summarizes a ticket rather than defining the product is the exception rather than the rule.

A page's `origination:` field overrides this per-page:

- `originate` (default) — the wiki IS canonical. Every page defining product intent: features, task flows, entities, PRDs, personas, positioning, product principles.
- `mirror` — canonical lives in Linear, Notion, or similar, and this page summarizes and points. Use it for the pages whose subject genuinely is a tracker artifact; the pointer must ride along. Refreshing it is manual. Its staleness threshold comes from the page's TYPE, not from this mode — `freshness:` on the page, else the wiki's `freshness.md` override for the type, else the type's own SLO in [[_authoring:wiki-page-types]]. A mirrored `prd` is therefore graded at the `prd` threshold like any other; set `freshness:` on the page when a tracker-backed subject needs a shorter clock.
- `link-only` — metadata + pointer only; no body. Rare in product; use when the external source is itself canonical and any wiki summary would drift.

## Authoring notes

**Product decisions and external pointers.** A product decision is recorded on a living product artifact, not a standalone `adr` (which is engineering-only): the scope cut or definition call captured directly in the `prd`, `feature`, or a `concept`. A decision *process* is a `daci-record` in `governance/`, which cites the product page it decided about. A Linear epic or Notion PRD is not a standalone page here — it rides as `origination: mirror` on the `feature` or `prd` page it backs, or on the governance `roadmap` when that is what it backs. See [[_authoring:wiki-authorship-routing#routing-table]].

A `data-model-entity` is a *logical* model and may be drafted while the design is still being settled and refined once it is built — the page can exist before its physical realization. Physical detail (indexes, column types, storage) lives in `engineering/`, not here.

## Cross-cutting backbone conventions

The pages named below are the homes these conventions assign, not pages every wiki already has: a young wiki has written none of them. Where one is not authored yet, carry the content inline on the page that needs it and move it when the backbone page appears — which is the same two-branch hedge the templates state (`… if authored; otherwise name it in prose`).

Product owns the *horizontal logic* that design and engineering pull hardest — captured on existing types, never new machinery. Downstream sub-wikis reference these; product never forward-links to them.

- **Access & permissions.** The governed role vocabulary is a `catalog` at `catalogs/roles.md`, the address the engine reads a role name against (a sitemap's Shown to, a journey's `roles:`) — *this project's capability-gating roles*, distinct from a `[[domain:entities/<actor>]]` domain-object (an industry business actor) and from a `persona` (a user archetype, not a permission grant). The role×capability matrix is an access/authorization-model `concept` (`concepts/access-model.md`), authored as product **intent** and linking the roles catalog; engineering *references* it and specifies enforcement — it never originates the model. Features, flows, and surfaces link the access-model where an action is role-gated. The access-model states *who may act*; the `no-permission`/access-gated resilience state renders the denial — don't duplicate the logic across the two.
- **Cross-cutting policies / business rules.** A rule spanning entities or features ("trials convert after 14 days", "one active subscription per account", "PII retained 90 days") is a product `concept` at `product/concepts/policies/<kebab-name>.md`, stated once and linking the governed `entities/`/`features/`. Per-entity invariants stay in the entity's `## Invariants`; per-capability and per-task rules stay in acceptance criteria (see the AC boundary). The rule lives here even when compliance-derived — operations' `compliance-record` holds only the *attestation* that a control is met, not the rule.
- **Measurement & instrumentation.** The analytics event taxonomy is a `catalog` (`catalogs/analytics-events.md`) — the governed vocabulary of *what is measured*; engineering's `system-entity` owns the persisted telemetry-record shape. A metric's *target* has one home, chosen by scope on the same rule as the NFR boundary below: bounded to one capability it lives in that `feature`'s `## Success metrics & instrumentation`, spanning a module or a release it lives in the `prd`. A *derived* metric's definition lives in an `algorithm` page. Dashboards stay in analytics tooling. A `feature`'s `## Success metrics & instrumentation` links the metric and names the events without restating the target or the formula.
- **Non-functional requirements (NFR boundary).** Product states the NFR *target/intent*: an attribute bounded to one capability lives in that `feature`'s `## Quality attributes`; one spanning a module or release lives in the `prd`'s Requirements. Engineering `architecture` pages own *system-wide* NFRs and their enforcement. This README is the canonical statement of the framework boundary — `feature`, `prd`, and the engineering README point here rather than restating it.
- **Features and set members (feature boundary).** A `feature` is a capability someone uses. A member of a governed set the capability works over — a check, a validation rule, a role, a notification event — is not a feature. This README is the canonical statement of the boundary — `feature`, `product-module`, `catalog` and `test-scenario` point here rather than restating it.
  - **The substitution test.** If adding one more member takes no new mechanism — only data, and at most a decision about that member — it stays a member. If it takes a new mechanism — behavior the capability does not already apply to every member — that mechanism is a feature, or a criterion on an existing one.
  - **Where a member's behavior lives.** The feature's acceptance criteria state the mechanism over the whole set. A member's own behavior is proven by the capability's tests over its fixtures, and no `test-scenario` row exists for a member alone. A member that one task triggers is a step of that task's flow.
  - **Where the set lives.** A set that meets the `catalog` template's Discipline is a `catalog`. A set only the code declares gets no page of its own: the feature's acceptance criteria describe it in the user's words.
- **Acceptance criteria (AC boundary).** A criterion lives where it can be verified. This README is the canonical statement of the boundary — `feature`, `task-flow` and `test-scenario` point here rather than restating it.
  - **Which page holds it.** One that spans a feature's flows, or states a capability-level commitment, lives in that `feature`'s `## Acceptance criteria`. One verifiable by exercising a single task lives in that `task-flow`'s.
  - **One home each.** Other pages cite the criterion's id and never restate it.
  - **Not a postcondition.** A flow's `## Postcondition` is the main path's end state. A guarantee that must hold on the alternate, error or anytime paths, or across repeated runs, is one of the flow's criteria instead.
  - **Write order.** A `feature` is written before its flows, so it holds every criterion until they exist; writing a flow moves its task-scoped criteria onto it, under the flow's own ids.
  - **Shared bases.** A shared base flow holds the criteria its specializations inherit, cited by its page path — `flows/_shared/<task>#AC<n>`, or `flows/<deliverable>/_shared/<task>#AC<n>` for a base only one deliverable's areas share; a specialization states only what it adds.
- **Scope boundaries (boundary statement).** [[_authoring:wiki-authoring-spec#boundary-statements]] is canonical for what a page's `## Boundaries` states, and for how it differs from `## Non-examples` and from a delegation section. What is product's own: a boundary bullet is not a second home for content the other entries in this list route — a policy rule, an entity invariant, a criterion, and a role gate each stay where those place them. A `prd` states the exclusion half under `## Out of scope` and names no neighbor. `task-flow` carries no boundary statement — its `## Delegated decisions` is what per-feature authors decide.
- **Resilience (app-ux).** How surfaces handle empty / loading / error / partial / access-gated states is a product-owned cross-cutting `concept` (`concepts/app-ux-resilience`) that design and engineering reference. *Accessibility*, by contrast, is design-owned — it lives in the design sub-wiki's `concepts/` and is referenced from there, not authored as a product page.

## Typical raw sources

Content flowing into `_raw/` that this sub-wiki references:

- Linear exports (epics, roadmap views)
- Notion PRDs and one-pagers
- Customer interview notes and transcripts (the research-grade write-up lands in `domain/`)
- Product strategy documents and memos
- Competitive landscape notes relevant to positioning

When research produces evidence used here, the primary landing page stays in `domain/` and product pages cross-reference via `[[domain:<path>]]` — the one outbound edge L1 has.

## When to originate, mirror, or link-only

- **Originate** when the artifact is product-function canon with no better tool — the narrative is the source. Product principles, and the scope rationale captured on the `prd`, `feature`, or `concept` it decides about.
- **Mirror** when Linear or Notion is the canonical home. Write a human summary; do not paste the full doc. Keep the summary short enough that staleness is obvious.
- **Link-only** when even a summary would drift faster than it is refreshed — rare in product. Prefer a tight `mirror` origination on the backing `feature` or `prd` instead.

Speculative features that are being explored but not committed should use the shared `concept` template under `concepts/`. Promote to `feature` once committed; archive the concept via redirect.

## What an engine checks, and what it does not

Rules in this file fall into the classes below, and the file does not otherwise distinguish them.

- **Checked, and an error.** Cross-wiki link resolution and the layer order (`/wiki-lint`), and a page's structure against its template — sections, declared table columns, block bullets, leftover placeholders (`/wiki-conformance-audit`). These fail a run and name the page.
- **Checked upstream, against the framework rather than your page.** The type list and the Subdir column in the table above are held to their sources by drift guards that run in agent-kit's own suite, not here. You see them as a failing build in that repo, never as a finding on your wiki.
- **Not read by any engine.** The default origination mode this README states is authoring guidance, not a value anything applies to a page: a page that sets no `origination:` is never flagged for disagreeing with the default. The same is true of which subdir a page of a multi-home type belongs in, and of every cell value inside a table whose columns are checked. These are review's job.

Run the two commands for the live list; neither this section nor any other file enumerates the checks, because a list maintained beside the thing it describes is the drift this wiki keeps closing.

## Retiring or relocating a page

Neither is a hand edit, and they are different operations.

- **Retiring** a page that others cite — run `/wiki-archive`. One invocation moves the page under `_archive/`, writes the `redirect` stub at the old path so every existing link still resolves, rebuilds `index.md` and the reverse citation index, and appends the `log.md` line. Follow it with `/wiki-lint`. Never write the stub by hand: `_templates/redirect-stub.md` is the scaffold for repairing a damaged stub, and a hand-copied one names an `_archive/` path nothing moved anything to while the original page stays live — two answers at two addresses.
- **Relocating** a page that is not being retired — run `/wiki-move`. It repoints the incoming links and leaves **no** stub, because a stub for a page that still exists is a second, stale answer to the same question.

Splitting and merging carry page-local ids across; the rules are in [[_authoring:wiki-page-ids#splitting-and-merging]].

## Cross-wiki reference syntax

Product's allowed outbound set is `domain/`, and nothing else.

- **Referencing other sub-wikis from a product page:**
  - Domain: `[[domain:entities/<slug>]]` — the entity a feature acts on; `[[domain:concepts/<slug>]]` for a shared term.
  - Research: `[[domain:synthesis/<slug>]]` — the evidence behind a persona or feature; `[[domain:sources/<slug>]]` for a single source.
- **Referencing within the product sub-wiki:** omit the prefix — `[[features/<module>/<slug>]]`, `[[personas/<slug>]]`.
- **Anchor syntax:** `[[domain:entities/cart#lifecycle]]` — anchor matches a header slug in the target page.

`/wiki-lint` validates all cross-wiki links when it is run — before a PR, or on a cadence. A broken link **or an out-of-hierarchy reference** is a lint error, not a commit block: nothing here is wired to a hook ([[_authoring:wiki-conventions#cross-reference-protocol]]).

## Using the `_templates/` files

`/wiki-init` copies everything under `_templates/` into the deployed `<wiki.location>/product/_templates/` so the templates travel with the sub-wiki. The local pool mixes universal product shapes with bd-flavored archive shapes that capture artifacts produced by the `domain-bd` workflows:

| Template | Page type | Target subdir | Source workflow |
|---|---|---|---|
| `feature.md` | `feature` | `features/<module>/` | (universal) |
| `app-base.md` | `app-base` | sub-wiki root | (universal) |
| `product-module.md` | `product-module` | `modules/` | (universal) |
| `task-flow.md` | `task-flow` | `flows/<module>/` | (universal) |
| `algorithm.md` | `algorithm` | `algorithms/` | (universal) |
| `data-model-entity.md` | `data-model-entity` | `entities/<module>/` | (universal) |
| `pr-faq.md` | `pr-faq` | `pr-faqs/` | `/working-backwards` |
| `prd.md` | `prd` | `prds/` | (universal) |
| `value-proposition.md` | `value-proposition` | `positioning/` | (universal) |

Note: `data-model-entity.md` carries `type: data-model-entity` (product-owned; the logical `## Data model` table shape), distinct from the domain sub-wiki's `domain-object` template (`domain/_templates/domain-object.md`), which carries `type: domain-object` (the industry actor-role flavor, prose Attributes).

Note: `retrospective` is homed in `governance/` and its template is local to that sub-wiki — it is not in the root `_templates/` pool. A product-cycle retrospective is authored there; an incident write-up is an `incident-record` in `operations/`.

`product-module.md` carries `kind`, `audience` and `platforms`. `kind` is **required** — the module's role, which the template defines and [[_authoring:wiki-page-placement#where-a-page-may-sit]] holds to its placement. `audience` (`customer` | `internal`) is **required** — always set it; it determines whether the module is product-facing or internal/ops. `platforms` (any subset of the surfaces the template lists) is **optional** — omit the line entirely when not yet decided. The `## Platform` prose section carries the nuance the list can't (e.g. which surface for which task).

To create a new page:

1. Copy the relevant template into the appropriate subdir (see table above).
2. Rename to `kebab-case.md` matching the page title.
3. Substitute placeholders: `{{TITLE}}`, `{{DATE}}`, `{{OWNER}}`, `{{CONFIDENCE}}`, `{{ORIGINATION}}` (one of `originate | mirror | link-only`; defaults to `originate` for product pages), plus any type-specific placeholders called out in the template header. **Exception:** every product-local page-template (`algorithm`, `app-base`, `data-model-entity`, `feature`, `prd`, `pr-faq`, `product-module`, `task-flow`, `value-proposition`) fixes `owner: product` by construction and omits `{{OWNER}}` — do not substitute it. `{{OWNER}}` applies only to the shared-pool templates (`concept`, `catalog`, `persona`).
4. Fill the body; leave section headers even when a section is empty (use "None." or remove only if the template says to).
5. Append a `log.md` entry: `## [YYYY-MM-DD] <op> | <title>`.

For `concept`, `catalog` and `persona` pages, use the shared templates under `_templates/` (relative to your wiki root — populated by `/wiki-init`); they are not duplicated here.

Some of what a page must say is not settled when it is written, and the grammar distinguishes the ways that can be true rather than collapsing them. A page whose SUBJECT has a lifecycle carries a typed `status:`. A section whose content arrives at a named later event is declared on the template's `Appends:` line and reads `Pending: <that event>.` until it does — never `None.`, which says the author considered it and had nothing to say. A page that is a register of items with their own states carries those states as columns. Which one applies is the template's to declare, not yours to choose; the full grammar is [[_authoring:wiki-page-state#page-state-axes]].
